thread:
pd-bot: :warning: PagerDuty: AUTOPAGE fired for service=redwood-inference-canary-health (alert: canary_error_rate_high)

sre-bot: auto-detected spike in 5xx rate on canary group 'rollout-2026-11' — error rate 18% over 5m, threshold 5%. Samples show grpc stream resets + kv-cache misses.

maria: acked oncall. i'm live. good catch. starting triage. tagging @ravi and @dan for deploy context.

dan: on it. i'm looking at the deploy pipeline. canary traffic currently at 12% global (staged ramp). this started ~3m after ramp to 10%.

jess: @maria please call a bridge if we think rollback is likely. i'll notify CS/ops. customers hitting inference timeouts? support-ops, any reports?

support-ops: seeing ~120 tickets mentioning timeouts in last 10m, mostly embeddings/large-seq requests. median latency up from 180ms -> 1.2s and error 504/ERR_STREAM_RESET. linking internal ticket IDs.

ravi: pulling canary pod logs now. kvcache warmup misses spike visible. suspected regression in kvcache eviction change from PR #4971. snippet from canary logs:

```
WARN kvcache: missing prefix key for req_id=abc123
ERROR model-serving: failed to attach kv cache: eviction mismatch
TRACE runtime: aten::allgather latency spike
```

maria: looks like the PR you mentioned landed into the canary image tag. can we diff config between canary and baseline? dan?

dan: config shows kvcache_eviction_policy=aggressive on canary, baseline=lazy. PR made default aggressive for memory savings. suspect regression under real traffic.

sre-bot: metric snapshot: canary_p99_latency +320% last 5m, canary_5xx_rate 18%, baseline 5xx_rate 1.1%. Risk: user-facing errors.

maria: immediate mitigation options: 1) roll canary back to previous image 2) flip kvcache_eviction_policy back to lazy via rollout config 3) throttle canary ramp to 0% (drain). preferences?

jess: CS says high-priority customers in EU are impacted. prefer fast rollback or traffic drain. we need to preserve logs for postmortem.

ravi: i can run a quick rollback to the previous image tag (v2026.11.3) — takes ~90s to apply and warm up. traffic switch is instantaneous but may still route to unhealthy pods until drained.

oncall-manager: Maria, handover? i'm available to take post-rollback verification once you start.

maria: go ahead, ravi — execute rollback. i'll coordinate verification. @pd-bot keep this page open until confirmed stable.

ravi: running rollback command now:
```
kubectl set image deployment/redwood-serving canary=registry.redwood/v2026.11.3 --namespace=prod
kubectl rollout status deploy/redwood-serving --watch
```

sre-bot: deploy event: rollback started by ravi at 3091234578. Auto-scaling paused during rollout.

dan: monitoring k8s events + LB health checks. p95 latency trending down after first replaced replica.

support-ops: ticket volume reduced ~40% after first 2 replicas replaced. CS inbox still getting a few reports.

maria: verifying end-to-end with a few golden prompts and embeddings. running synthetic test suite against canary ip.

maria: synthetic checks: all green. p50/p95 latency back to baseline, error rate dropping to 0.8% on canary group.

sre-bot: rollback complete at 3091234589. canary image back to v2026.11.3. canary_error_rate down to 0.9%.

jess: ✅ Notifying CS and impacted customers that we rolled back and are monitoring. Patch PR #4971 flagged for revert and deeper kvcache testing.

maria: handing off to @oncall-manager for post-incident verification and postmortem lead. thanks @ravi @dan for quick action.

oncall-manager: taking handoff. i'll run a 1h watch and collect logs/metrics. please drop any extra findings in this thread. we'll open a postmortem doc and include reproducer and blameless timeline.

ravi: filing a revert PR now with test additions for kvcache eviction under cold-start and long-seq requests. reference: PR-rollback-3091234567.

support-ops: CS updated customers at 3091234594. close tickets after watch window if no regressions.

maria: closing the paging loop: will mark PD incident as resolved once 30m stable. leaving this thread open for notes. :white_check_mark:
